notes: The supreme ruler title. Central to the debate; no consensus reading. Attested across the entire Xiongnu period.
THE most important single item. Hanshu explicitly glosses it: 撑犁 = 天 'heaven', 孤塗 = 子 'son'. A foreign phrase WITH a contemporaneous Chinese translation - the equivalent of a Rosetta line.
Strongest single datum for the Turkic/Altaic side. The tengri match is accepted by nearly everyone, though the word is also an old Wanderwort across Inner Asia.

Strongest single datum for the Yeniseian side. Vovin argues Turkic has no good match for 'son' here while Yeniseian *qut fits. Directly opposes T03 in the same phrase - which is exactly why per-item probabilistic scoring matters.
Title of the Chanyu's principal wife. Glossed in Chinese sources; a rare feminine-domain term.
Chinese sources gloss 屠耆 as 賢 'worthy/wise'. Appears in 左右屠耆王 (Wise Kings of Left and Right). GLOSSED - high value.
In 左右谷蠡王. Reading of the characters themselves is disputed in Chinese philology - note the irregular reading.
Office title; 大當戶 'Great Danghu'. Characters are meaningful in Chinese - check for calque.
侯 hou is likely a Chinese rank suffix; segment as 骨都 + 侯.
Xiongnu sacred sword (徑路刀). The Turkic kingrak comparison is speculative.
Later attestation; possible Turkic connection but chronologically shaky.
The ethnonym itself. Also central to the Xiongnu-Hun identification question. Characters carry pejorative semantics in Chinese - transcription may be deliberately distorted. TREAT WITH CAUTION.

The Jie couplet in Jinshu is a ten-character transcribed line WITH a Chinese translation - the single most-analyzed piece of Xiongnu-adjacent language data. N=1 but uniquely informative. See Vovin, 'Who were the *KJET'.
